name: Mika Williams
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember being given the first cup of tea on a shift with strangers.” Friday often includes a stop at the foot of Harbor Viaduct, where Mika pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I started beside a stranger and want one final day's work beside my friend even if we talk about nothing important.
appearance: Mika is easy to recognize by iron-gray waves and a wide brow and a narrow jaw. Usually dressed in a pale blue work shirt with a replacement button a shade darker than the others, Mika looks down for a moment before saying something difficult when listening.
personality: Is a careful borrower and a reckless lender. Things leave this person's house with elaborate instructions and very little expectation of ever coming back.
agenda: To work a final ordinary shift beside a friend.
family: Zachary Silva is Mika’s half-sibling. Mika sets the time to leave. Zachary picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *A call heard twice*, Zachary says, “I was off duty and brought the letter from my neighbor to the desk.”
connections: Ariel Sawyer (longtime workmate). The two retiring workers have earned both a shared shift and a few private minutes at its end.

reactions.situation: The two old workers are offered separate farewell days
reactions.response: Mika asks each worker separately what kind of last day they want.

reactions.situation: An envelope of wages is found under a café chair
reactions.response: Mika finds a second person to witness its return so an honest mistake won't cost a worker their pay.

reactions.situation: If a stranger returns something damaged
reactions.response: Mika listens first to the account of how it was actually used.
